learn.title: India EV Policy: PM e-DRIVE Explained
learn.intro: India's transport sector drives 14% of national CO2 emissions, making EV adoption critical. The PM e-DRIVE scheme and state-level subsidies are accelerating electric mobility, targeting cleaner cities, reduced oil imports worth billions, and positioning India as a global EV manufacturing hub.
learn.c1_text: Launched in 2024, PM e-DRIVE allocates ₹10,900 crore to deploy 3.2 million EVs across segments. Think of it as a fuel subsidy flip: instead of subsidising petrol, the government discounts electric two-wheelers up to ₹10,000 and buses significantly, making upfront prices competitive.
learn.c2_text: States compete to attract EV factories through road tax exemptions, registration waivers, and charging infrastructure mandates. Delhi waives road tax fully, while Tamil Nadu offers capital subsidies of up to 30% on plant investment, creating regional manufacturing clusters alongside automotive supply chains.
learn.c3_text: India targets one charging station every 3 km in cities. Programmes under state DISCOMs support over 72,000 public chargers, with 22,000 already installed nationwide. Bengaluru and Delhi lead deployment, addressing range anxiety that previously deterred buyers transitioning from petrol vehicles.
learn.stat1: India EV market: 1.9 million units sold cumulatively by 2024
learn.stat2: PM e-DRIVE budget: ₹10,900 crore ($1.3 billion) for EV deployment
learn.stat3: Target: 3.2 million EVs to be supported under PM e-DRIVE
learn.stat4: Two-wheeler share: ~60% of India's domestic EV sales in 2023

learn.title: Perovskite Solar Cells: Beyond Silicon
learn.intro: Perovskite materials could push solar cell efficiency past 30% while slashing manufacturing costs. These printable, flexible crystals promise lightweight panels for windows, vehicles, and rooftops where rigid silicon struggles, potentially revolutionising how and where solar electricity is generated.
learn.c1_text: Perovskite refers to a crystal structure (ABX3) that absorbs light exceptionally well. Imagine painting solar cells instead of soldering them: perovskite inks can be roll-to-roll printed on flexible plastic, costing potentially one-tenth of silicon wafer production while using abundant raw materials.
learn.c2_text: Single-junction perovskite cells jumped from 4% efficiency in 2009 to over 26% by 2024. Tandem stacks pairing perovskite atop silicon have reached 34%, surpassing the 29% silicon-only theoretical Shockley-Queisser limit by harvesting different wavelengths like a two-tiered waterfall.
learn.c3_text: IIT Bombay and IISc Bangalore lead Indian perovskite research, targeting tropical humidity resilience. India aims to prototype domestically manufactured perovskite-silicon tandem modules by 2027, supporting the 500 GW non-fossil target through next-generation solar tailored for high-temperature operations.
learn.stat1: Record efficiency: 34.6% for perovskite-silicon tandem cells (2024)
learn.stat2: Cost potential: perovskite could reach $0.10 per watt vs silicon $0.30
learn.stat3: Efficiency growth: from 4% (2009) to 26%+ (2024) in 15 years
learn.stat4: Stability goal: commercial cells need 25-year operational lifetimes

learn.title: Solid-State Batteries: Safer Power
learn.intro: Solid-state batteries replace flammable liquid electrolytes with solid materials, enabling higher energy density and eliminating fire risks. They could double EV range, slash charging times, and transform grid storage, making electric vehicles lighter and dramatically safer.
learn.c1_text: Unlike lithium-ion's liquid electrolyte, solid-state uses ceramic or sulfide materials. Think of it as replacing a swimming pool with a solid sponge: ions still move, but there's nothing to leak, burn, or explode, fundamentally changing battery safety architecture and thermal management.
learn.c2_text: Solid-state batteries can use lithium metal anodes, packing 400-500 Wh/kg versus today's 250-300 Wh/kg. An EV driving 400 km today could theoretically travel 700+ km on the same weight, while smartphone batteries double their runtime without increasing size.
learn.c3_text: India's PLI scheme allocates ₹18,100 crore for advanced chemistry cell manufacturing. Tata and Reliance are piloting solid-state production, targeting import reduction. ISRO transfers lithium-ion expertise while Indian startups explore indigenous solid electrolyte formulations, building supply chain sovereignty.
learn.stat1: Energy density: solid-state targets 400-500 Wh/kg vs 250-300 current
learn.stat2: Temperature range: operates safely from -30°C to 100°C
learn.stat3: India PLI budget: ₹18,100 crore for advanced battery manufacturing
learn.stat4: Cycle life: prototypes achieving 1000+ charge-discharge cycles

learn.title: Direct Air Capture: CO2 Removal
learn.intro: Direct Air Capture (DAC) machines extract CO2 directly from ambient air using chemical processes, offering geological-scale carbon removal. Unlike trees, DAC works anywhere, anytime, and provides permanent sequestration, complementing emissions cuts needed to meet global climate targets.
learn.c1_text: DAC facilities use giant fans pulling air through chemical sorbents that bind CO2 molecules, similar to how a sponge soaks water. The captured carbon is then heated, concentrated, and compressed for underground storage or utilisation in fuels, creating negative emissions at gigatonne scale.
learn.c2_text: Leading DAC plants like Iceland's Orca and Mammoth run on geothermal and hydro energy, ensuring removal is genuinely carbon-negative. Each facility consumes around 2,000 kWh per tonne of CO2 captured, equivalent to powering 60 homes, demanding clean baseload power integration.
learn.c3_text: India's CSIR labs are developing low-cost DAC sorbents tailored for tropical humidity. With 2.4 billion tonnes of annual emissions, India could deploy DAC in industrial corridors, pairing with steel and cement sectors. Costs currently hover at $400-1000 per tonne but could fall below $100.
learn.stat1: Operating plants: 27 DAC facilities worldwide capturing 0.5 Mt CO2/year
learn.stat2: Energy use: ~2,000 kWh needed to capture one tonne of CO2
learn.stat3: Iceland's Mammoth: captures 36,000 tonnes CO2 annually
learn.stat4: Cost target: reduce from $600 to under $100 per tonne by 2030

learn.title: Electric Buses and Trucks Electrified
learn.intro: Heavy-duty vehicles cause disproportionate emissions despite being fewer in number. Electric buses and trucks offer 60-80% operating cost savings on fuel and maintenance, plus dramatic emission cuts. Commercial fleet electrification is accelerating as battery prices fall and charging networks mature.
learn.c1_text: A typical diesel bus costs ₹35 per km to run while an e-bus costs ₹12. With India's FAME-II scheme subsidising e-bus procurement, cities like Mumbai and Bengaluru are deploying 900+ electric buses, saving crores annually while reducing urban air pollution affecting millions of commuters.
learn.c2_text: Electric trucks need megawatt chargers and 600+ km range batteries. Hydrogen fuel cells offer faster refuelling for long routes, while battery-electric suits regional haulage. Tesla Semi, BYD, and Tata are racing to deliver 40-tonne e-trucks with 500+ km capabilities within this decade.
learn.c3_text: India plans 50,000 e-buses under PM e-DRIVE by 2030. Delhi, Bengaluru, and Hyderabad lead depot-based charging deployments. The National Electric Bus Programme targets 100% public transport electrification in major cities, supported by 700+ e-bus manufacturing under PLI automotive scheme.
learn.stat1: Diesel bus cost: ₹35/km vs e-bus ₹12/km operational savings
learn.stat2: Target: 50,000 electric buses to be deployed in India by 2030
learn.stat3: Emission cut: e-bus saves 1.5 tonnes CO2 per year per vehicle
learn.stat4: Global e-bus stock: exceeded 600,000 units worldwide in 2023

learn.title: Solar Panels Compared: Types Guide
learn.intro: Choosing solar panels affects system cost, efficiency, and rooftop space needed. Monocrystalline, polycrystalline, and thin-film technologies each offer distinct advantages. Understanding differences helps homeowners, businesses, and utilities select the right panel for their specific installation conditions.
learn.c1_text: Made from single-crystal silicon, mono panels achieve 20-24% efficiency, the highest commercially available. Think of them as premium chocolate: more refined, smoother appearance, smaller footprint. They perform better in low light and last 25-30 years, making them ideal for space-constrained urban rooftops.
learn.c2_text: Poly panels use melted silicon fragments, giving them a distinctive blue speckled look. Efficiency ranges 15-18%, with lower manufacturing cost making them 10-15% cheaper than mono. They're the reliable mid-range option, offering good value for large installations with ample rooftop space.
learn.c3_text: Thin-film panels deposit photovoltaic material onto glass, plastic, or metal at 1% the thickness of silicon. While only 10-13% efficient, they outperform in high heat and shaded conditions, suiting India's tropical climate. Bhadla Solar Park uses thin-film for cost-effective utility-scale generation.
learn.stat1: Mono efficiency: 20-24% vs poly 15-18% vs thin-film 10-13%
learn.stat2: Cost difference: poly panels 10-15% cheaper than monocrystalline
learn.stat4: India solar capacity: 90 GW installed, 64% ground-mounted (2024)
